P001.text: Treat the overnight export pipeline as a dynamic system.

P002.text: The proposed input is the maximum number of concurrent exports in a small worker pool; outputs are queue depth, completion rate, elapsed export times, and queue, object-read, and upload durations where observable.

P003.text: This assumes concurrency is adjustable and a canary pool can be bounded safely; neither capability is established by the packet.

P004.text: Before testing, establish worker versions, trace coverage, active work, initial queue depth, and available workload descriptors.

P005.text: Use only already scheduled overnight exports, with no customer-requested business-hours reruns.

P006.text: If a bounded experiment is unavailable, defer the perturbation and choose a deployment that supplies the necessary controls and comparable telemetry.

P007.text: First verify comparable queue-entry, worker-start, and completion timestamps across the versions being compared.

P008.text: If these are missing, deploy narrowly scoped instrumentation and collect an overnight baseline before testing performance changes.

P009.text: With adequate telemetry, record a baseline at concurrency c0, then at a documented time apply one known step to a lower concurrency c1 in the canary pool and hold it constant.

P010.text: Select the step size and cohort size beforehand from available capacity and overnight deadline headroom; a reduction tests the hypothesis that contention contributes to delays, without assuming it does.

P011.text: Let active exports finish and record when actual concurrency reflects the new limit.

P012.text: Keep worker version and other controllable settings fixed.

P013.text: Where feasible, retain an unchanged comparison pool with comparable scheduled work; record shared-resource exposure and workload differences.

P014.text: Record the trajectory through the transition and subsequent observation window.

P015.text: Predeclare queue-age, backlog-growth, error-rate, resource-pressure, and completion-deadline thresholds, plus a latest rollback time that preserves recovery headroom.

P016.text: If a threshold is crossed or telemetry fails, restore c0 without terminating active exports, stop further experimental exposure, and monitor recovery.

P017.text: At the planned endpoint, restore c0 and follow exposed exports to completion where feasible; explicitly censor any still unfinished.

P018.text: Measure the delay from the commanded step to actual concurrency change and then to changes in queue depth, completion rate, and phase durations.

P019.text: Look for the size and speed of changes, transient peaks or oscillations, and whether outputs settle into a sustained range or keep drifting.

P020.text: Compare export cohorts by queue-entry time and exposure to the step, retaining exports already active at the transition as a distinct group.

P021.text: Track the fraction exceeding one hour and time-to-completion estimates that include unfinished exports, alongside the stable-median question.

P022.text: Compare these trajectories with baseline and any unchanged pool.

P023.text: Missing spans must remain unknown, not zero-duration phases.

P024.text: Record arrivals, workload mix, worker version, and observed resource conditions alongside the response so that coincident changes are visible.

P025.text: These are proposed measurements, not observations already obtained.

P026.text: If actual concurrency falls and object-read or upload durations subsequently improve relative to comparable baseline and control work, that supports a contention-sensitive explanation at the tested load.

P027.text: It supports a deployment decision only if total export delay, throughput, and deadline risk also remain acceptable.

P028.text: If service phases remain similar while queue delay increases, reduced capacity is a better explanation of that response and the lower limit should not be expanded.

P029.text: If improvement is sufficiently precise to meet a predeclared operational benefit criterion without violating safety criteria, choose a staged, monitored rollout of the tested concurrency setting with rollback available.

P030.text: If it worsens outcomes, restore the original setting and reject that change.

P031.text: If results are inconclusive, retain the original setting and either repeat the bounded test on later scheduled nights or deploy instrumentation for the unresolved phase.

P032.text: These results constrain candidate mechanisms; they do not by themselves justify blaming or rolling back a particular worker version.

P033.text: The reported roughly five-percent slow-export rate makes short tests potentially uninformative.

P034.text: Set the observation duration and precision requirement before testing using available overnight volume and the smallest operationally meaningful improvement; if the safety window cannot supply enough evidence, report uncertainty rather than extending exposure unsafely.

P035.text: Unknown initial backlog, changing arrivals, heterogeneous workspace sizes, cache state, shared storage or network disturbances, version-dependent trace gaps, and interacting jobs can distort the response.

P036.text: A nominal concurrency step may take effect gradually while active work drains.

P037.text: Shared resources can contaminate a comparison pool, and nonlinear saturation can make one step behave differently from another.

P038.text: Apparent settling requires a sufficiently stable workload and adequate observation time; otherwise describe only the observed transient.

P039.text: No detectable change does not exclude contention or a version defect.

P040.text: Conclusions apply to the tested cohort, concurrency range, versions, and operating conditions; broader deployment requires staged confirmation.
